title: Animal Record-Holders
keyIdea: A record-holder beats every other animal at one thing. The cheetah is the fastest on land, at about 100 km/h, and the peregrine falcon is the fastest of all when it dives. The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived, about as long as 5 cars. The giraffe is the tallest, about 3 grown-ups high, and the bee hummingbird is the smallest bird, shorter than your thumb. Big does not mean fast, and heaviest does not mean tallest.
familyTip: Make a blue whale outside. Take 25 big steps in a line: that is about 25 m, as long as a big blue whale. Then find a doorway: a giraffe is nearly 3 doorways tall. Ask: which record would you like to hold, fastest, tallest or smallest?

visual.caption: Which record does each animal hold? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: race animals on land, race a falcon dive, line up cars by a blue whale, tape a giraffe, put birds in size order.

kid: A record-holder is the best in the world at one thing. Fastest means faster than all the others. Tallest means taller than all the others.
The cheetah is the fastest animal on land. It can run as fast as a car on a big road. The elephant is huge, but it is slow. Big does not mean fast.
The peregrine falcon is even faster. It dives down from the sky to catch its food. So the cheetah is the fastest on land, and the falcon is the fastest of all.

The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived. It is about as long as 5 cars, and heavier than any dinosaur. The giraffe is the tallest, about 3 grown-ups high. The bee hummingbird is the smallest bird. It is shorter than your thumb.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This links naming and comparing common animals (KS1 science) with comparing lengths, heights and speeds (Year 1 and 2 measurement). Key words: record, fastest, biggest, tallest, smallest, heaviest, faster than, about, km/h. An "-est" word means more than every other one, so a record is always about one thing.

Rounded figures: a cheetah sprints at about 100 km/h for short bursts; a racehorse about 70 km/h; the fastest person ever, Usain Bolt, peaked at about 44 km/h; an elephant manages about 25 km/h. A peregrine falcon dives at more than 300 km/h, though it flies much slower on the level. The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived: up to about 30 m long and well over 100 tonnes, heavier than any known dinosaur. The Natural History Museum's blue whale skeleton, Hope, is 25 m long. A giraffe reaches about 5.5 m. The bee hummingbird is about 5 to 6 cm long and weighs under 2 g; the ostrich, the biggest bird, stands about 2.5 m.

Common mistakes: thinking the biggest animal must be the fastest; calling the cheetah the fastest animal of all, when it holds the land record; thinking the biggest animal ever was a dinosaur; and thinking the heaviest animal is also the tallest. Be careful with pictures too: books often draw a hummingbird and an ostrich the same size. Say "about", because animals vary.

In the lab your child races a cheetah, a horse, the fastest person and an elephant, races a falcon dive against a cheetah, lines up cars beside a blue whale, slides a tape up a giraffe and an elephant and counts grown-ups, and puts four birds in size order from smallest to biggest.

practice.prompt: A car is about 5 m long. How long is a line of {a} cars, nose to tail?
practice.hint: Add 5 m for every car in the line.
practice.explain: {a} cars of about 5 m make about {=a*5} m. A big blue whale is about 25 m: 5 cars.

practice.prompt: There are {a} animals in a race. The cheetah wins. How many animals does the cheetah beat?
practice.hint: The winner beats every animal except itself.
practice.explain: The cheetah beats all the others: {a} take away 1 is {=a-1}. That is what fastest means.

practice.prompt: Which animal is the fastest on land?
practice.hint: Think of the race. Who got to the flag first?
practice.explain: The cheetah can sprint at about 100 km/h. The horse is fast too, but slower, and the elephant came last.

practice.prompt: Which is faster: a cheetah running, or a peregrine falcon diving?
practice.hint: Remember the race from the sky in the lab.
practice.explain: A peregrine falcon dives at more than 300 km/h, about 3 times as fast as a cheetah runs.

practice.hint: Think of the tape in the lab. Whose head was highest?
practice.explain: A giraffe is about 5.5 m tall, about 3 grown-ups. An elephant is heavier but only about 3 m tall.

pool.prompt: What is the biggest animal that has ever lived?
pool.hint: It is alive today and lives in the sea.
pool.explain: The blue whale is the biggest animal ever: about 25 m long, heavier than any dinosaur.

pool.prompt: Which is the smallest bird in the world?
pool.hint: Its name has a tiny insect in it.
pool.explain: The bee hummingbird is about 5 cm long: shorter than your thumb. The ostrich is the biggest bird.

pool.prompt: A bee hummingbird is about 5 cm long. How long are {a} bee hummingbirds in a line, beak to tail?
pool.hint: Each bird adds about 5 cm to the line.
pool.explain: {a} birds of about 5 cm make about {=a*5} cm in a line.

pool.prompt: An ostrich is about 250 cm tall. A child is {a} cm tall. How many cm taller is the ostrich?
pool.hint: Take the child's height away from 250.
pool.explain: 250 take away {a} is {=250-a}, so the ostrich is about {=250-a} cm taller.

pool.prompt: Is the biggest animal in a race always the fastest?
choices: No: the elephant is big but slow
Yes, if it has long legs
pool.hint: Think of where the elephant came in the race.
pool.explain: No. The elephant is big but came last. The cheetah is much smaller and is the fastest on land.

pool.prompt: Finish the sentence: the cheetah is the fastest animal ...
pool.hint: Is there anything faster in the sky?
pool.explain: The cheetah holds the land record. The peregrine falcon is faster when it dives from the sky.

pool.prompt: An elephant is heavier than a giraffe. Which one is taller?
pool.hint: Heaviest and tallest are different records.
pool.explain: The giraffe is taller, about 5.5 m. The elephant is heavier, but only about 3 m tall.

pool.prompt: A book shows a bee hummingbird and an ostrich drawn the same size. What is true?
pool.hint: Pictures are drawn to fit the page.
pool.explain: An ostrich is about 2.5 m tall. A bee hummingbird is about 5 cm. Pictures are not real size.
